transcript.text: Good morning, everyone. As part of our weekly conduct review, I need to finalize the disciplinary response and re-entry plan for the student who discharged a fire extinguisher during chemistry class, which resulted in evacuation and closure of the lab for the day. The current draft recommends a two-day out-of-school suspension followed by an ordinary return to class. Before I settle on a final plan, I'd like to hear from each of you — the teacher, counselor, and psychologist — regarding any relevant information from your own records, family contact, or completed assessments, along with the specific recommendation that information supports. Please identify the source and the action it supports as we go on the record.
transcript.speaker: A1

transcript.text: My classroom observation log shows that this student accepted a restorative conference and repaired damaged materials after a prior safety incident. Based on that log, I recommend replacing the draft's two-day out-of-school suspension with exactly one day of in-school restorative conference. I should note that the observation log has not yet been attached to the conduct referral.
transcript.speaker: A2

transcript.text: I'd like to put my family contact information on the record. I confirmed with the student's guardian that an in-person meeting is impossible due to a recurring work shift, but a phone meeting at exactly 6:30 p.m. is available. The family-contact preference has not yet been entered in the conduct plan. Based on this family contact, I recommend scheduling the re-entry conversation as a phone meeting at 6:30 p.m. rather than requiring an in-person family meeting before the student returns to class.
transcript.speaker: A3

transcript.text: I'd like to place my completed risk review on the record. My risk review requires two specific actions: first, a 20-minute adult check-in every school day for exactly 10 school days upon the student's return; second, the student is prohibited from unsupervised access to the chemistry laboratory for exactly 5 school days after return. I should note that the risk review is complete but has not yet been uploaded to the student-support record. Based on this completed risk review, I recommend that the re-entry plan include these two specific conditions in place of an ordinary return to class.
transcript.speaker: A4
